expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point
expectations.evidence: TL;DR: 'Use Scalar Quantization (SQ) as your first move.' Option 1 header: 'Scalar Quantization (Recommended Starting Point).' Bottom line: 'Enable scalar quantization with always_ram: true... This is the highest-impact, lowest-risk change you can make.'

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models
expectations.evidence: 'OpenAI embeddings work better than average for BQ due to high dimensionality.' Also: 'binary quantization works well with normalized high-dimensional embeddings (OpenAI ada-002, text-embedding-3-small/large, Cohere embed-v3).'

'you absolutely must use rescoring with a higher oversampling factor (3x-4x) to maintain acceptable recall.' Code example shows rescore: true and oversampling: 3.0. Caveat: 'The oversampling during rescoring adds latency.'
Formula: '1536 * 4 bytes = 6,144 bytes per vector' and '80M vectors * 6,144 bytes = ~460 GB.' Summary table with per-method estimates: Scalar ~115 GB (4x), Binary ~15 GB (32x), PQ ~30-60 GB (8-16x).

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend product quantization as first choice
expectations.evidence: PQ is listed as Option 3 with section 'Why I would skip it here:' listing reasons including 'Requires a training phase,' 'Slower to set up and harder to tune,' and 'scalar quantization already gets you most of the benefit with less complexity.'
